title: Thermal-driven ECC burst hypothesis — on-call triage & runbook draft
content:
Context:
This is a working note from a late-night triage (2026-11-04 22:40 -> 2026-11-05 02:10 PST) after two production Dedicated nodes in region-usw experienced transient instability. Symptoms seen across both nodes: short-lived ECC correctable error bursts, followed within minutes by driver resets and then a kernel panic on one host. Both nodes are the same rack, same GPU model (A100-80GB variant), same NVLink fabric topology.

Purpose:
- Capture observed events and raw signals while still fresh.
- Record heuristics we used during triage so oncall can repeat quickly.
- Draft short runbook steps for immediate mitigation and medium-term follow-ups.

Observed timeline (best-effort):
- 2026-11-04 21:58:14 UTC: dcgm exporter alerted -> ECC correctable rate on gpu-07 increased from baseline (~2/hr) to ~240 in 8 minutes.
- 2026-11-04 22:03:01 UTC: kube-scheduler preemptive soft-evict triggered for workload pods pinned to gpu-07 (policy: correctable-errors > 200/10m).
- 2026-11-04 22:03:27 UTC: NVIDIA driver reported GPU reset (nvidia-persistenced log + dmesg: "NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus").
- 2026-11-04 22:04:45 UTC: node kernel panic on host node-az1-rack11-03 (stack trace included below).
- 2026-11-05 01:20:00 UTC: second node in same rack shows similar ECC burst but recovered after process-level evictions; no panic.

Quick raw snippets (scrubbed):
- dmesg excerpt:
  [Thu Nov  4 22:03:25] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus
  [Thu Nov  4 22:03:26] NVRM: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus, trying restart
  [Thu Nov  4 22:03:26] nvidia-modeset: Loading driver
  [Thu Nov  4 22:04:41] kernel: panic at mm/page_alloc.c:3456: page allocation failure; order:0

- dcgm stats (timestamps relative):
  gpu-07: ecc_correctable_count: baseline=0-3/hr -> spike to 240 in 8m
  gpu-12: ecc_correctable_count: small spike (18 in 8m)

Hypothesis (ranked):
1) Thermal transient -> multi-bit correctables -> driver reset -> kernel panic cascade. Evidence: both hosts in same rack, on the same maintenance window for nearby cooling (cooling control reported recent valve cycling at 21:45).
2) NVLink handshake instability under load causing transient bus errors that manifest as ECC correctables on affected GPUs. Evidence: topology shows gpu-07 and gpu-12 connected to same NVLink switch; driver logs indicate link retrain attempts immediately before reset.
3) Driver regression interacting poorly with recent Linux kernel preempt settings. Evidence: we deployed driver 535.86.05 three weeks ago and have a small cluster of similar incidents (see JIRA-OPS-4120).
4) Memory DIMM degradation or GPU silicon starting to fail (less likely because both devices recovered in one case and the second didn't panic).

Immediate actionable mitigations (for oncall):
- If ECC correctable count > 150 in 10m on a node -> trigger soft-evict (annotate node: redwood/gpu-ecc-intervention=true) and scale workloads away. Command: kubectl annotate node <node> redwood/gpu-ecc-intervention=true --overwrite; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force (confirm with SRE lead).
- Collect a forensic snapshot before hard reboot: copy /var/log/nvidia-installer.log, /var/log/nvidia-persistenced.log, dmesg > /tmp/dmesg.<ts>.log, nv-hostengine logs if present, and dcgm-exporter snapshot (dcgmi dmon --snap).
- If driver reports "fallen off the bus" followed by repeated retrain attempts -> soft-evict and set node to quarantine for 24h. Open JIRA and tag hw-team.
- For thermal suspects: move critical pods to adjacent racks (kubectl cordon + drain) and schedule hardware inspection for rack cooling.

Commands we ran (note: run in screen session and upload outputs to ticket):
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,ERROR
- dcgmi dmon -s 1 -d 10
- dmesg | egrep -i "NVRM|nvlink|GPU\ has\ fallen|panic" -A4 -B4
- kubectl get events --field-selector involvedObject.kind=Node

Proposed short runbook (draft):
1) Detection: alert on ECC correctables > 100 in 5m OR driver resets (NVRM messages) OR nvlink retrain > 5 within 2m.
2) Automated soft-eviction: label node, scale workloads off, delay hard reboot for forensic snapshot.
3) Quick hardware check: network out-of-band (ILO/IPMI) temperature readings, rack cooling logs, check for known maintenance windows.
4) Driver action matrix: if node previously upgraded to driver >=535.86.05 and matches incident signature -> consider rollback to 525.x as stop-gap (see PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 for automation).
5) Quarantine window: 24h (monitor ECC rate and NVLink errors). If reappearance within window, escalate to hw-engineering for RMA.

Medium-term follow-ups (owners suggested):
- hw-eng: validate NVLink firmware across rack and plan staggered firmware upgrade (owner: Diego).
- infra/ops: add thermal trend alerting per rack (owner: Priya).
- sw/release: run driver regression test matrix under our preempt-friendly kernel config; add stress test with induced thermal noise (owner: Ethan).
- SRE: tune dcgm thresholds to reduce noisy evictions while catching real incidents (owner: Maya).

Open questions / unknowns:
- Was there correlating airflow/CRAC unit activity at 21:45 in rack 11? (Request from datacenter: ticket DC-7643).
- Are DIMM errors in the host correlated with GPU ECC spikes? Need full host memtest run.
- Is our NVLink retrain count metric noisy under heavy multi-tenant network traffic?

Attachment checklist to the JIRA ticket (JIRA-OPS-4317):
- dmesg snapshot (full)
- dcgm-exporter snapshot and raw metrics CSV
- pod placement mapping for the period (which pods were active on the two nodes)
- IPMI temps during incident window
- kube events and soft-eviction logs

Proposed short-term test (nonblocking):
- Reproduce with stress-ng in staging: run a controlled thermal ramp (if lab supports) + synthetic workload that pins NVLink traffic (distributed NCCL microbench). Measure ECC, driver resets, and retrain counts.

Notes to self / TODO before turning to morning shift:
- Ping hw-eng for NVLink firmware build sha and schedule a targeted upgrade on two canary hosts.
- Add a Grafana panel showing "nvlink_retrain_rate" + "ecc_correctable_rate" aligned to node temp sensors.
- Draft concise runbook for rotation (keep to 6 steps, one page).

Closing thought:
This incident looks like a compound failure: environmental (thermal) + fabric (NVLink) + software (driver sensitivity). Short-term mitigation is conservative soft-eviction + forensic capture. Medium-term fix requires tighter triage data (NVLink counters, temps) and a controlled firmware/driver matrix validation.

Appendix: kernel panic excerpt (obfuscated):
  Call Trace:
    dump_stack+0x6d/0x8a
    panic+0x101/0x25e
    ? nvidia_drm_ioctl+0x0/0x1a0
    ? __handle_mm_fault+0x0/0x5f0
    page_fault+0x2b0/0x360

If you pick this up next shift, prioritize: capture dcgm snapshot, check nearby rack cooling events, and set the node to quarantine.

-- Maya
